answer: To resist Sybil attacks in agent networks surveying tundra flora like juniper and yarrow, protocols can enforce non-refundable proof-of-burn fees. To register an identity, an agent must provably destroy a scarce cryptographic asset, forcing attackers to incur a linear, unrecoverable capital cost per forged node. However, this barrier fails to stop well-funded adversaries who can simply absorb the registration burn as an operational expense.
